observed_fact: Coinbase reported that criminals bribed and recruited rogue overseas support agents who abused customer-support access and stole data
source_assessment: Coinbase stated that the data was used to facilitate social-engineering attacks and that the company received a USD 20 million extortion demand
my_assessment: Legitimate support access can be converted into criminal intelligence that increases the success of customer fraud without directly exposing private keys or passwords
confidence: High for company-reported facts; moderate for the full criminal structure
alternative_explanation: Different insiders may have had different knowledge or intent and public reporting may not describe all access paths
decision_relevance: SOC, fraud, insider-risk, HR, procurement, legal and customer-support teams need a shared investigation model
source: Coinbase — Protecting Our Customers: Standing Up to Extortionists

observed_fact: FBI IC3 reported global BEC exposure exceeding USD 55 billion and continued use of banks, payment processors and cryptocurrency services
source_assessment: FBI describes BEC as compromise or impersonation of trusted business identities used to cause unauthorised transfers
my_assessment: The decisive control point is often the payment or supplier-change workflow rather than the email filter alone
confidence: High for the scale and fraud model
alternative_explanation: Complaint data may underreport or inconsistently classify incidents and not every loss involves mailbox compromise
decision_relevance: Email, identity, supplier-master and payment data must be correlated and recall action must begin quickly
source: FBI IC3 — Business Email Compromise: The USD 55 Billion Scam

observed_fact: FS-ISAC and Akamai reported finance as the top target for volumetric DDoS attacks and described a multi-bank attack with multi-day outages
source_assessment: The report assessed that DDoS had evolved from nuisance activity into a strategic operational threat
my_assessment: Financial institutions should detect material service degradation and customer impact rather than alerting only on traffic volume
confidence: High for sector reporting; moderate when generalising to every organisation
alternative_explanation: High traffic may reflect legitimate demand and some attacks may produce little disruption
decision_relevance: DDoS monitoring must connect network telemetry to customer transactions, service levels, provider dependencies and DORA resilience processes
source: FS-ISAC and Akamai — From Nuisance to Strategic Threat

observed_fact: The European Supervisory Authorities designated critical ICT third-party providers in November 2025
source_assessment: The designation process considered systemic importance, support for critical financial functions and service substitutability
my_assessment: Supplier concentration is now an active supervisory concern as well as a technical threat-model issue
alternative_explanation: Designation does not mean that a provider is insecure or that all clients face identical risk
decision_relevance: Financial entities need dependency registers, contractual evidence, exit strategies and incident coordination for critical providers
source: European Banking Authority — DORA critical ICT third-party provider designation

observed_fact: Current standards and tools support structured CTI, automated exchange, behaviour mapping and portable detection formats
source_assessment: OASIS, MITRE, MISP and Sigma provide complementary models for representing intelligence and translating it into defensive operations
my_assessment: The value of CTI is measured by validated searches, detections and decisions rather than the volume of received indicators
alternative_explanation: Tools may be deployed poorly and automation may amplify low-quality intelligence
decision_relevance: Every shared indicator requires context, confidence, lifecycle and testing before automated enforcement
source: OASIS STIX/TAXII; MITRE ATT&CK; MISP; SigmaHQ
